These books are a value and treasure greater than a college education in comparative mythology and religious studies ever could be. Give yourself the keys of discernment. Listen to Spirit Whirled.

recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Body: Kyle and Serena Denton are community herbalists creating wild-crafted and organic plant medicines out of Milwaukee since 2015. I have used their teas and tinctures on an almost daily basis for years now. Kyle is a great friend of InnerVerse and has appeared on the channel more times than I can count. These products work, not in the allopathic "pharma-medicine" way, but in a terrain-support, consciousness bolstering plant-teacher sort of way.

recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.
recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Name: The Sonic Slider

recEBEDXpPbvCxQw5.Body: Melissa Kupsch is the Australian homeopath behind RMDY Collective and RMDY Academy of Homeopathy, and one of the clearest voices I know for homeopathy as true energy medicine. Her remedies work on the resonance principle, like cures like, where a matching frequency from nature is shown to the body so the vital force can recognize the distortion and resolve it. When Melissa joined Kyle Denton and me on InnerVerse, we explored the premise that spirit precedes form, and homeopathy demonstrates that principle as plainly as anything I know. RMDY makes quality remedies and first aid kits accessible, prepared with real care for who makes the medicine and how.
recEBEDXpPbvCxQw5.Name: RMDY Collective

I use LotusWei Elixirs to give me an edge with psychic & energetic sensitivity, discernment, and life force coherence. recMVdJjP2VZJyI2m.Body: Clive de Carle has spent decades researching high-quality natural health essentials, from magnesium and fulvic minerals to iodine, selenium, and vegan-sourced vitamin D. His supplements are formulated with a focus on bioavailability, so the body can actually absorb and use what you're taking rather than letting it pass through unused. It's a simple, no-nonsense approach to filling the nutritional gaps most modern diets leave behind.

rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Name: Chance Garton

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Sound healing and remote tuning fork work", "body": "Chance described his Biofield Tuning practice, in which tuning forks are swept through the aura while he imagines the client lying on a massage table. He explained that the work rests on non-locality, so sessions can run over distance when both people agree to them. He said the biofield has a distinct anatomy, that unhealed trauma and ancestral hang ups tend to sit to the left or right of the body, and that Eileen McKusick's books taught him the method. He argued that healing is worth paying for, and that calling the result placebo does not mean it did not work."}, {"title": "Astrology as math, wheel and geometry", "body": "Dan Shukis explained astrology as a measure of divine timing based on planets moving at predictable speeds, with a birth chart as a snapshot of the sky at the first breath. He stressed that everyone contains all twelve signs on a 360 degree wheel. Chance added that the zodiac is man made and that sidereal and tropical systems both have value, then screen shared pages from Marty Leeds on Phi, the Fibonacci sequence and a repeating cycle of 24. Dan tied it together as sacred geometry, music theory and the circle of fifths."}, {"title": "Divination as an art with a bias", "body": "The group asked whether astrology and tarot are too subjective. Dan said every reader brings a lens, so a conspiracy minded astrologer and a woke one will read the same chart differently, and that the craft combines a logical structure with a creative, interpretive side. Chance said he prefers reading for strangers because it keeps him more objective. Jen and Joe compared this to improvising in the kitchen, such as making cinnamon buns without a recipe, and the guests compared healers who invent protocols with practitioners who just follow an insurance script."}, {"title": "The matrix as womb, fate and free will", "body": "Chance suggested that birth is a cut on the timeline that traps people in the legal matrix, and floated the idea that life is an embryonic dream before a death that works like another portal. The guests noted that matrix comes from the Latin for a breeding female and relates to mater and matter, and Chance mentioned Nick Hinton's Saturn Time Cube Matrix. Dan said a birth chart is fixed, while Chance argued that knowing it lets a person get ahead of the wave."}, {"title": "A live tarot spread and winter forecast", "body": "At the host's closing question about where things are headed, Chance pulled cards on air, including the five of cups, the four of pentacles, the death card and the king of swords. He read them as mourning, a turn toward growing food and building real wealth, the end of old ideas and a failed push toward the metaverse and digital money. Dan added a forecast from the Venus retrograde on Pluto in Capricorn on December 19 and the United States Pluto return, predicting a hard winter, financial trouble, and an easier spring."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: I joined Jen and Joe from Legit Bat and also Dan Shukis from Cosmic Keys. We had a fun chat about astrology and other occult correspondences. It was laid back, but there was plenty of gravy here.
